name: How an acceptance criterion is born, built & retired
summary: The data flow of an acceptance criterion through the AC-driven pipeline: a plain-language request is triaged, the authoring agents (PO → BA → IT PO) write the AC records into the store, you approve each stage, the scanner surfaces ready ACs, a wired ticket is generated, and once its implementation merges the AC is marked done automatically. Around that spine sit the update paths — scope stays locked to the author, existing code is discovered and back-linked, ACs can be re-homed without breaking references, and retiring an AC forces its code to be reconciled.

steps.label: Triage the request
steps.human:
A new feature request enters through /plan-feature; a fast triage agent classifies it (strategic / behavioral / technical / covered) and checks the store for duplicates before any AC is written.

I/O boundary: The feature request is plain text. The JSON input projection represents parsed AC YAML; triage emits the prompt-defined JSON decision. Example IDs are illustrative, not a routing receipt.

steps.label: Author the AC tree (PO → BA → IT PO)
steps.human:
The workflow runs the authoring agents in sequence — the Product Owner writes L0/L1 value, the Business Analyst decomposes them into L2/L3 Gherkin, the IT PO adds the technical fields — writing AC YAML records into the store, never into ticket files.

I/O boundary: PO/BA/IT PO persist YAML files. The shown JSON is their schema-checked parsed-record representation, not a newly introduced API.

steps.label: Review, approve & commit each stage
steps.human:
You confirm each authoring stage before the next agent runs; on approval the AC's readiness advances and the stage's output is committed to git, so the store moves forward one reviewed step at a time.

I/O boundary: Human approval is conversation input; the structured output is the AC YAML readiness field. Git commit identity is a separate Git artifact; no approval or commit is executed by this example.

steps.label: Scan the store for ready work
steps.human:
The scanner walks the store for todo, unblocked leaf ACs and presents them as a prioritized backlog of what can be built next.

I/O boundary: scan_ac_store.py reads and ranks existing records. This projection describes fields of each eligible AC, not a new serialized ranked-backlog envelope; ordering is scanner output.

steps.label: Generate a wired ticket
steps.human:
For a chosen ready AC the generator produces a fully-wired ticket and writes the implemented_by back-reference onto the AC, so the ticket and the AC point at each other.

I/O boundary: generate_ticket_from_ac.py writes Markdown ticket content/frontmatter and an AC YAML backlink. The shown fields cover the AC side; the ticket is a Markdown document, not a JSON ticket DTO.

steps.label: Implement, then mark the AC done
steps.human:
Once the implementing ticket merges, the AC store is updated automatically — mark_ac_done sets work_status to done and a post-merge hook flips every AC the completed ticket covered.

I/O boundary: mark_ac_done.py and post-merge processing mutate AC YAML after the actual merge. Illustrative output does not certify that any AC is complete.

branches.condition: an implementation agent tries to change an AC's scope
branches.label: Scope stays locked to the author
branches.human:
Only the requirement's author can change what 'done' means; implementation agents may report progress via work_status but not rewrite the criteria, and every change is traceable to the agent that made it.

I/O boundary: The hook compares staged record fields and emits diagnostics plus a process exit code. It does not serialize a new approval object; a passing example is not authorization.

branches.label: Discover & link existing code
branches.human:
When implementing code already exists, the audit matches it to the AC by exact-criteria text and backfills the covered_by / implemented_by links instead of generating a duplicate ticket.

I/O boundary: The audit reads repository files and writes declared evidence links into parsed AC YAML. File references are declarations, not successful execution receipts.

branches.label: Re-home without breaking links
branches.human:
Each AC has a permanent id independent of its place in the tree, so a requirement can be moved to another component with a single change and every existing reference keeps working.

I/O boundary: Moving the AC YAML file/component preserves its id; filesystem placement is not a new JSON transport.

branches.label: Retire & reconcile the code
branches.human:
Retiring an AC triggers a check that the code it claimed is actually gone, so a deprecated requirement can't quietly leave live code behind.

I/O boundary: Retirement checks source file evidence and returns a gate diagnostic/exit status. The deprecated YAML record is an input, not evidence that referenced code was actually removed.

acceptance_scenarios.then: it is classified and checked against the store for duplicates before any AC is authored

acceptance_scenarios.when: the authoring agents run in sequence
acceptance_scenarios.then: L0-L3 acceptance criteria are written to the AC store and never to ticket files
the AC's readiness advances and the stage output is committed to git before the next agent runs
every todo, unblocked leaf AC is surfaced as prioritized ready work

acceptance_scenarios.when: a ticket is generated from it
acceptance_scenarios.then: the ticket is fully wired and the AC records the implemented_by back-reference

acceptance_scenarios.given: an implementing ticket that has merged
acceptance_scenarios.then: the covered ACs' work_status is set to done automatically

acceptance_scenarios.given: an implementation agent editing an AC
acceptance_scenarios.when: it tries to change the criteria text
acceptance_scenarios.then: the change is rejected unless it is the author, and any allowed change is attributed to the agent that made it

acceptance_scenarios.given: an AC whose implementing code already exists
acceptance_scenarios.then: the implementation is matched and linked via covered_by/implemented_by instead of generating a new ticket

acceptance_scenarios.given: an AC referenced from many places
acceptance_scenarios.when: it is moved elsewhere in the tree
acceptance_scenarios.then: its permanent id keeps every existing reference working
leftover code the AC claimed blocks the commit until it is reconciled
